Hi team,

What we have observed:
- Error rate spike to ~28% (5xx and connection resets)
- Median latency jump 120ms -> 1.2s, p95 > 3s
- Persistent for 20+ minutes and not improved after local retries

We are attaching a small sample of request ids and traces (northstar_latency_samples.zip) and a quick KPI snapshot (kpi-snap.csv). Please escalate — our ops and execs are asking for a mitigation plan and ETA. If you need to route traffic elsewhere, we need guidance and an expected window.

Please confirm receipt and next steps.

—Elena

Quick triage notes:
- No active node replacement events in us-west-2 cluster during 07:30–08:10 PST in infra events log. Autoscaler showed normal activity.
- Kernel/driver updates: none in that window.
- I see a spike of request queue depth on the us-west-2 serving pool for the customer-specific priority route. Queue depth correlates with the observed latency bump.
- Attaching a short tail log extract inline below for Diego.

> [08:00:03] serve-pool-usw2-03: accept loop delayed, queue depth 128
> [08:01:12] serve-pool-usw2-03: 5xx from runtime: KV_CACHE_MISS(transport)
> [08:02:07] serve-pool-usw2-02: grpc stream disconnects increased

Prelim conclusion: backlog amplification on the priority route + increased KV cache churn causing cascading latency and 5xx. Not yet a hardware outage.

If we can't bring queue depth down by 08:50 PST, recommend immediate traffic handoff.

-Hannah

Subject: Re: [NorthStar] URGENT: sudden throughput collapse in us-west-2 — impacting checkout

Thanks — dug into runtime traces. Key findings:
- Several model shards for the customer's pinned variant experienced KV cache hot-set churn between 07:44–07:58 PST; cache misses surged causing extra backend fetches and increased token latencies.
- Memory pressure triggered GC-like stalls on two serving instances (serve-pool-usw2-02 and -03) around 07:59–08:03 PST; these correlate with 5xx spikes.
- No network flaps detected at infra layer (BGP/cloud connector stable).

Mitigation steps taken (now):
- Increased per-instance token-processing threads on serve-pool-usw2-01/04 to help drain backlog.
- Disabled aggressive KV prefetch on the customer route to reduce churn risk.

If backlog does not drop by 09:10 PST, I'm +1 on an ordered handoff to us-west-1 with staged rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) and slow-start TTL to avoid cold-cache spikes.

Diego
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime

Elena — quick update and next steps (executive summary for your leadership):

What we observed: backlog amplification on your priority route in us-west-2 around 07:45–08:05 PST, causing KV cache churn and GC-like stalls on two serve instances which generated elevated 5xx. We confirmed infra/network stable — this was runtime load amplification.

Action taken:
- Attempted in-region mitigations (thread increase, reduce prefetch) — partial improvement but p95 still elevated.
- At 09:15 PST we executed a staged cross-region handoff to us-west-1 (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with slow-start warmup.
- Traffic normalized within ~9 minutes of full shift. 5xx rate returned below 1% and median latency dropped back to ~140ms.

Customer impact & credits:
- Incident lasted ~2 hours from first observed to stable cross-region; impacted checkout success rate for ~35 minutes during peak.
- We're prepared to offer a one-time service credit and a short-term priority routing SLA for the next 72 hours. Jonas, please advise on credit approval process.

Attachments: pd-incident-1234.txt (timeline), northstar_latency_samples.zip, kpi-snap.csv

Next steps:
- Diego/Hannah to run a post-mortem focusing on KV cache sizing and slow-start warming thresholds; share findings within 48 hours.
- Vanessa/Sales to coordinate customer comms and credit proposal.
- I'll schedule an exec sync with NorthStar for Monday to review mitigation and compensatory measures.

Elena — sorry for the disruption. We'll follow up with a detailed RCA and the post-mortem action items.

Thanks,
